about: A message as SES v2's SendEmail takes it, as FF reads and makes it: the table the backend's L1 (email-send.spec.ts and ses-operations.spec.ts) and ff local's mail read for their tests, so that both read a request alike and make the same message of it. `addresses` are lists as a header or the API writes them, each address in lower case, null for one that is no address; `senders`, a sender's one address, null for none or more than one; `headers`, a request's own header and why it can't be the message's, null when it can; `raw`, a raw message's sender and its recipients' fields as its header writes them, unfolded, and the message without its Bcc. `composed` is simple content made into a message, as a reader shows it: each header field's value unfolded, its encoded words decoded, `{id}` the message's ID and `{host}` the SES endpoint's; the fields it hasn't; its type, and each part's type and body, decoded, its line breaks \n and the last dropped. `written` is how the backend's nodemailer writes a field, which ff local needn't: the backend's alone. `routes` are SES v2's that FF answers, each operation by its method and path, a name in the path decoded; null for one FF doesn't answer. `requests` are SendEmail's bodies, each checked in FF's order before the account's state is read: `refused`, with SES's status, error and words; `taken`, with the message's sender and its recipients, each once, in lower case, as its envelope names them. `manyTo` stands for that many recipients in ToAddresses, r1@example.tn and on; a raw message given as `message`, its text, is sent as `Data`, in base64.
